name: minesweeper
title: Minesweeper
description: The mine-clearing game in the panel, on its own page: the mouse as in the original (click, right-click, both buttons), or one hand on the keys (the arrows move, Enter opens, / flags, N starts over, D picks the level). The board, the clock and the best times persist.
author: pal

settings.label: Difficulty
settings.description: The board's size and mines, also picked on the board itself (D, or a click on the level). Applies to the next board, at once when nothing is open yet; a game in progress plays out first.

settings.label: Clock
settings.text: Show the time while you play
settings.description: Off hides the time beside the face. Your times still count for best times and show when you clear a board. Also T or ⌘K in the game.

store.tagline: Minesweeper in the panel: the classic board, by mouse or one hand on the arrows
features: The classic board redrawn: square raised cells that press flat, the numbers in their classic colours tuned for the light and dark panel, an LED mine counter and clock around the face
Mouse as in the original: click opens, right-click flags, a click (or both buttons, or the middle one) on a satisfied number opens around it; a held button shows the cells it would open pressed
One-handed: the arrows move the cursor, `Enter` opens, `/` (just above the arrows) flags; `hjkl`, `F` and `Space` do the same, `N` starts over, `D` picks the level
The classic rules: the first open is always safe and opens an area, an empty cell floods open, a satisfied number opens around it
An open ripples out from the cell as the caps lift; a mine goes off with a blast and the rest pop out from it; a cleared board plants its flags under confetti
Beginner 9 by 9, intermediate 16 by 16, expert 30 by 16, each with a best time and a won count; the board scales to the panel, compact included
The clock runs from the first open and only while the board is on screen; Escape leaves at any point and the game is there when you come back, across restarts
T hides the clock if it rushes you; your times still count

screenshots.caption: Mid-game on beginner: the mine counter, the face and the clock, the best time and the won count, the keys under the board
Cleared: the mines left are flagged, the time, a new best, confetti
A mine went off on intermediate: every mine shows, a wrong flag is crossed out
Expert, 30 by 16 with 99 mines, scaled to the panel; Enter on the satisfied 2 opens around it

actions.title: Open
actions.description: On a number whose flags are all placed, opens the cells around it. A new game once the game is over.

actions.title: New game
actions.description: A fresh board; asks first mid-game. A click on the face starts one at once.

actions.title: Difficulty
actions.description: The level picker: left and right choose, Enter takes it (asking first mid-game), D again closes it.

actions.title: Hide the clock
actions.description: No running time on screen; again to bring it back. Times still count.

minesweeper.description: The board, the extension's own page. Escape leaves mid-game; the board and the clock wait for you.

keys.title: Move (also down, left, right, and hjkl)
Open; on a satisfied number, open around it; a new game once the game is over
